prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision: A fairer, greener UK built on rapid climate action, properly funded public services, reduced inequality and strengthened democracy.

Health and social care
- Rebuild a fully public NHS; oppose privatisation. Rapid GP access, universal NHS dentistry, cut waiting lists, fair pay and retention for staff.
- Extra NHS revenue: +£8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years.
- Invest in primary care, community diagnostics, public health (restore £1.5bn), and mental health (28‑day access to therapies; counsellors in every school/college).
- National Cancer Plan; support assisted dying with safeguards; end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: free personal care; career pathways and fair pay; £20bn/yr investment.

Homes and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/year; end Right to Buy; bring empty homes back into use.
- Renters: local rent controls; end Section 21 no‑fault evictions; stronger dispute resolution.
- Retrofit and resilience: £29bn to insulate homes to EPC B (10‑year plan), £9bn for clean heat, £7bn to adapt to heat, £4bn for public buildings.
- All new homes to Passivhaus‑equivalent with solar and low‑carbon heating; protect Green Belt; people‑centred planning.

Energy and climate
- No new oil and gas; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax rising from £120 to up to £500/tonne within 10 years.
- Target ~70% electricity from wind by 2030; lift onshore wind barriers; 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar by 2035.
- Expand grid, storage and interconnectors; support green hydrogen for necessary uses.
- Community ownership in new renewables; oppose new nuclear; phase out existing.

Economy and tax
- Green economic transformation: average £40bn/yr investment (rail electrification, public transport, retrofits, water/sewage, industry decarbonisation).
- Public ownership: rail, water, and Big 5 energy retailers.
- Fair taxation: wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn), align CGT and investment income with earnings, remove NI upper limit, inheritance and property tax reform; stronger anti‑avoidance.
- Carbon tax to fund transition; no basic rate income tax rise; borrow to invest within inflation constraints.

Work and welfare
- Workers’ rights charter; repeal anti‑union laws; day‑one rights; equal rights for gig workers; 10:1 pay ratio cap; £15/hr minimum wage with SME support; move toward four‑day week.
- Social security: +£40/week to UC/legacy benefits; scrap two‑child cap, sanctions and bedroom tax; 5% uplift to disability benefits; protect triple lock; raise Carer’s Allowance; long‑term Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; 30% land/sea for nature by 2030; re‑wet peat; expand woodlands; right to roam; nationalise water; boost regulators’ budgets.
- Animal protection commission; ban blood sports, factory farming practices, snares and lead ammunition.
- Food: universal free school meals and breakfast clubs (primary); triple farm support to shift to nature‑friendly, mixed farming; expand UK horticulture; cut ultra‑processed foods and waste.

Education
- End tuition fees; restore grants; invest in FE/skills; £8bn for schools (+£2bn teacher pay), £2.5bn/yr to fix unsafe buildings; £5bn for SEND; de‑stress assessment; bring academies under local control; VAT on private school fees.

Transport
- Public transport first: free bus travel for under‑18s; annual rail/bus subsidies rising to £10bn; £19bn over five years for public transport and active travel; £2.5bn/yr for cycling/walking; rail in public ownership.
- Oppose new roads; road pricing; 20mph default in built‑up areas; phase‑out new petrol/diesel sales by 2027; accelerate EVs and charging.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Proportional representation; repeal Elections Act; replace House of Lords; votes at 16; stronger lobbying transparency and media standards; defend Human Rights Act; support self‑ID for trans people.
- Migration: end hostile environment and NRPF; safe routes; right to work while awaiting asylum; simplify visas; remove spousal income rules.

Justice
- Restore trust in policing; curb stop and search and facial recognition; invest in courts/legal aid; presumption against short custodial sentences; expand restorative justice; make misogyny a hate crime; decriminalise personal drug possession.

Foreign policy
- Support Ukraine; pursue ceasefire, recognition of Palestine, end UK arms sales to Israel; increase aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; back Loss and Damage fund; rejoin EU (Customs Union first); sign UN nuclear ban, cancel Trident; reform NATO toward peace-building.
